solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Control over key Australian bank

indicators.note: the word for control is laid over the other pieces, covering them on both sides

parts.note: to hold sway is to have control
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge of a key Australian bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is a verb here, as in banking money, not the financial institution the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to save money up secretly or for later, a verb sense of bank.

clue.text: Replace whip

definitions.meaning: to exchange one thing for another
a thin flexible cane or rod

explanation.surface: Swap the whip.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for swapping and a noun for a slender rod used to beat.

clue.text: Computer literacy primarily applicable at work

indicators.note: first and foremost, so the first letter of literacy

parts.note: apt means suitable, relevant
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Computer literacy is chiefly useful in the workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable personal machine is one type of computer.

clue.text: Loves commercials featuring old soldiers

indicators.note: the commercials feature the soldiers, holding them within

parts.note: ads are advertisements
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: Someone is fond of adverts starring veterans.
explanation.definitionFit: To adore is to love deeply, a direct synonym in the third person.

clue.text: Improve when playing Thora, homeless, in French film

indicators.note: the reworked letters go inside the film title

parts.note: Amelie is a 2001 French film starring Audrey Tautou

indicators.note: the letters are played with, put in a new order
without home, which is H, so that letter is taken away

explanation.surface: An actress named Thora, without a home, improves a French film by appearing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'homeless' means losing H, the usual abbreviation for home; 'playing' then shuffles what is left. Amelie is a 2001 French film.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is to make better, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Appear unexpectedly with power to stop infectious disease

indicators.note: a stopper goes into the neck of a bottle, so this piece is plugged inside the disease

parts.note: croup is a childhood respiratory infection
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Something shows up, bringing the power to halt an epidemic.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to arise or occur without warning.

clue.text: Account for Republican euphoria

parts.note: elation is great happiness

explanation.surface: A report of the Republicans celebrating.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a narrative, as in relating a story.

clue.text: Clever PA involved with the PM at one time

indicators.note: the letters are tangled up together

explanation.surface: A smart assistant working with a former Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Spencer Perceval was the British Prime Minister assassinated in 1812.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the only British premier to have been assassinated, a past holder of the office.

clue.text: Punch-up involving everyone left in game

indicators.note: the reversed punch takes in the other piece
in a down answer up means reading backwards

parts.note: to lamp someone is slang for to hit them
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out with everyone gone from a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch-up' looks like one word for a brawl, but splits into Punch and the reversal signal 'up'. Pall-mall was an old mallet-and-ball game that gave the London street its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pall-mall was a historical lawn game like croquet.

clue.text: Hesitation after Peto's support becomes irregular

indicators.note: the hesitation sound is placed after the setter's support, at the end

parts.note: Peto is the setter, so Peto's is I'm, I am
a prop holds something up
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: The setter hesitates when his support goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name; here 'Peto's' stands for I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something not in keeping with rules or accepted standards.

clue.text: More than one found in river to the east of Poland

indicators.note: in an across answer east is to the right, so the river follows the Poland letters

parts.note: PL is the international vehicle code for Poland
the Ural flows through Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: A geography fact: something found in a river east of Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has a real geography joke: the Ural river does lie well to the east of Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a word form denoting multiple things is the plural form.

clue.text: Irritable clergyman touring Ohio regularly

indicators.note: the clergyman goes round, enclosing the other letters

parts.note: a cleric is a member of the clergy

indicators.note: every other letter of Ohio is taken, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A grumpy vicar on a tour of Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of Ohio, and 'touring' sets them just after the clergyman's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Choler was the humour of anger, so the word describes someone bad-tempered.

clue.text: Burn flag after queen leaves

indicators.note: the queen departs, so her letters are removed from the flag

parts.note: a streamer is a long narrow flag or pennant
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone sets fire to a flag once the monarch has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burn' looks like setting fire, but a burn is the Scottish word for a small river or brook.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and northern England a burn is a brook or small watercourse.

clue.text: Conjecture not originally indicating embezzlement

indicators.note: without its original, first letter

parts.note: speculation is guessing

explanation.surface: Guesswork that does not really point to fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculation is the theft of funds entrusted to one, especially public money.

clue.text: Fight to get charge withdrawn following French exam online

indicators.note: the free-of-charge piece is followed by the rest, coming first in the answer

parts.note: with the charge taken away something is free
an oral is a spoken examination
read as on line: L for line, put on (beside) the exam

explanation.surface: Someone takes an online French exam that suddenly costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'online' splits as 'on line': L (line) set next to ORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl that everyone joins in is a chaotic open fight.

clue.text: Settled for Frank

definitions.meaning: of debts or accounts, square, paid up

explanation.surface: Choosing someone called Frank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' poses as a name, but it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both squared up, of accounts, and honest or candid.

clue.text: Believe after former Labour leader gets a grip

indicators.note: the believe word comes after the leader's name

parts.note: Michael Foot led the Labour Party from 1980 to 1983
to hold a view is to believe it

explanation.surface: A former Labour leader takes a firm hold of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A secure grip or position from which to advance or climb.

clue.text: I admit describing refusal as rude

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so the admission goes round

parts.note: I grant means I admit
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that a refusal was impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in the geometric sense of drawing round.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant is used colloquially to mean ill-mannered or impolite.

clue.text: Carefully considered even if taking Tevez initially on loan

parts.note: though means even if

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the footballer's name is used

parts.note: a library book on loan is out

explanation.surface: A football transfer: Tevez arriving on loan, a deal planned with care.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlos Tevez is an Argentine footballer who played in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that has been well planned in advance has had full deliberation.

clue.text: Modest honour worthless? Not at first

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British honour

indicators.note: the first letter is not there

parts.note: waste describes something unwanted and of no value

explanation.surface: A question whether a modest honour is worth anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at first' drops W from WASTE to give ASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste and modest both describe someone pure and decorous in behaviour.

clue.text: Slender girl's bottom pinched by horse doctor in the middle of Ossett

indicators.note: the built piece sits inside the two central letters
just the central pair of letters of the town name
squeezed inside the vet's letters

parts.note: a vet treats horses

indicators.note: in a down answer the bottom is the last letter of girl

explanation.surface: A slim girl gets nipped by a horse vet in a Yorkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ossett is a town in West Yorkshire; 'in the middle of' does double duty, picking its central pair of letters and putting the rest between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Svelte means slim and graceful, a synonym.

clue.text: Consisting of temporary accommodation by design

parts.note: made up in, as in a statue in bronze
a tent is a temporary shelter

explanation.surface: Someone lives in a tent on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Intent is purpose or aim, as is design in the phrase by design.

clue.text: Fighting to get something done

definitions.meaning: military combat, as in soldiers seeing battle

explanation.surface: Fighting as the way to get things done.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both combat and any deed performed.

clue.text: Make heavy demands on port in Jersey for instance

parts.note: to tax someone is to strain them
a haven is a harbour

explanation.surface: Demands placed on a port in Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is a Channel Island with low taxes, which is why it fits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jersey is an example of a low-tax jurisdiction attracting offshore money.

clue.text: Comprehensive's attempt to introduce Latin faces party backsliding

indicators.note: the attempt brings in the Latin letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a go is a try

indicators.note: sliding back, so the party's letters run in reverse

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party

explanation.surface: A comprehensive school tries bringing in Latin while the party backtracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive' suggests a British state secondary school, but it is an adjective; 's is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean all-embracing, covering everything.

clue.text: Collapse emotionally seconds after girl gets to explain

indicators.note: the seconds letter comes after the girl's name

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
to solve a mystery is to explain it

explanation.surface: A girl finally manages to explain things.
explanation.definitionFit: To be overcome, as in breaking down in tears or laughter.

clue.text: Left-leaning party embraced by poet until now

indicators.note: held inside the poet's name

parts.note: Nahum Tate was a Poet Laureate

indicators.note: in an across answer leaning left means running backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A poet who has taken up with a left-wing party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left-leaning' reads as politics but turns DO into OD.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means so far, up to the present time.

clue.text: Concern for butcher in Street

indicators.note: to butcher something is to hack it about, so the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: A worry for a butcher with a shop on the high street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butcher' looks like a noun but is a verb, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A concern can be a business stake or a matter of attention, both senses of the word.
